completed.doc:
**Mellin–Barnes integral, DLMF 24.7.11**: for `0 < c < 1` and complex `x`,
`Bₙ(x) = (1/(2πi)) ∫_{-c-i∞}^{-c+i∞} (x+t)ⁿ (π/sin(πt))² dt`, written along `t = -c + is`.

completed.name: DLMF.Combinatorics.hasSum_narayana
completed.doc:
DLMF 26.6.8: `∑_{n,k=1}^∞ N(n, k) xⁿ y^k = (1 - x - xy - √((1-x-xy)² - 4x²y))/(2x)`, for
sufficiently small real `x ≠ 0` and `y`.

completed.name: DLMF.Confluent.whittakerM_besselJ_series
completed.doc:
The Whittaker–Buchholz expansion of `M_{κ,μ}` in Bessel functions of consecutive orders
(DLMF 13.24.2). The generating-function recurrence determines the sum through the normalized
Whittaker equation, and the principal powers cancel term by term.

completed.name: DLMF.QHypergeometric.qPochhammer_root_ratio
completed.doc:
The `k`-th root analogue of the very-well-poised factor, with `ω` a primitive `k`-th root of
unity (DLMF 17.2.E23).

completed.name: DLMF.QHypergeometric.qPhi_coefficient_classical_limit
completed.doc: Formal coefficient limit in 17.4.2, with its integer phase/scaling exponent.

completed.name: DLMF.QHypergeometric.qPhi_finite_classical_limit
completed.doc: The finite limit retains bottom poles that occur only after the final retained term.

completed.name: DLMF.QHypergeometric.qPsi_coefficient_classical_limit
completed.doc: The bilateral limit is formal/coefficientwise; its analytic annulus collapses as q→1.

completed.name: DLMF.QHypergeometric.one_phi_zero_common_zeros_removable
completed.doc: Common product zeros have a removable germ, rather than the quotient totalization 0/0.

completed.name: DLMF.Struve.lommelCapital_parameter_limit
completed.doc: Existence of the limiting definition at exceptional parameters.

completed.name: DLMF.Weierstrass.HalfPeriods.weierstrassZeta_fourier
completed.doc:
DLMF 23.8.2 (with the corrected condition `|ℑ(z/ω₁)| < 2ℑτ`), `z ∉ 𝕃`:
`ζ(z) - η₁z/ω₁ - (π/(2ω₁))cot(πz/(2ω₁)) = (2π/ω₁) ∑_{n≥1} q^{2n}/(1 - q^{2n}) sin(nπz/ω₁)`.
Corrected from the printed DLMF formula: the absolute value on `ℑ(z/ω₁)` is missing in the
printed condition, as in 23.8.1; without it the series diverges.

completed.name: DLMF.Weierstrass.HalfPeriods.weierstrassP_fourier
completed.doc:
DLMF 23.8.1 (with the corrected condition `|ℑ(z/ω₁)| < 2ℑτ`), `q = e^{iπω₃/ω₁}`, `z ∉ 𝕃`:
`℘(z) + η₁/ω₁ - (π²/(4ω₁²))csc²(πz/(2ω₁)) = -(2π²/ω₁²) ∑_{n≥1} nq^{2n}/(1 - q^{2n}) cos(nπz/ω₁)`.
Corrected from the printed DLMF formula: the printed condition lacks the absolute value on
`ℑ(z/ω₁)`; for `ℑ(z/ω₁) ≤ -2ℑτ` the series diverges (terms `10⁵, 10¹¹, 10²¹` at
`n = 10, 20, 40`).

completed.name: DLMF.Weierstrass.HalfPeriods.weierstrassSigma_sin_prod
completed.doc:
DLMF 23.8.7: `σ(z) = (2ω₁/π) exp(η₁z²/(2ω₁)) sin(πz/(2ω₁))
∏_{n≥1} sin(π(2nω₃ + z)/(2ω₁)) sin(π(2nω₃ - z)/(2ω₁))/sin²(πnω₃/ω₁)`, `z ∈ ℂ`.

completed.name: DLMF.Weierstrass.HalfPeriods.weierstrassSigma_prod
completed.doc:
DLMF 23.8.6: `σ(z) = (2ω₁/π) exp(η₁z²/(2ω₁)) sin(πz/(2ω₁))
∏_{n≥1} (1 - 2q^{2n}cos(πz/ω₁) + q^{4n})/(1 - q^{2n})²`, `z ∈ ℂ`.
Convergence and the product identity are stated separately so zeros of the sine prefactor
are retained. Dividing by that prefactor would incorrectly assert product value zero at `z=0`.

newHelpers.name: DLMF.BernoulliEuler.bernoulli_mellinBarnes_sin_ne_zero
newHelpers.doc:
The sine denominator of the Bernoulli Mellin–Barnes kernel has no zeros in the strip
`-1 < Re z < 0`.

newHelpers.name: DLMF.BernoulliEuler.bernoulli_mellinBarnes_differentiable
newHelpers.doc: The polynomial Mellin–Barnes kernel is holomorphic between its two neighboring pole lines.

newHelpers.name: DLMF.BernoulliEuler.bernoulli_mellinBarnes_sin_strip_lower
newHelpers.doc: The real sine factor stays uniformly away from zero on a closed subinterval of `(-1, 0)`.

newHelpers.name: DLMF.BernoulliEuler.bernoulli_mellinBarnes_tail_bound
newHelpers.doc:
On a closed substrip of `-1 < Re z < 0`, the polynomial Mellin–Barnes kernel has an
integrable bound of order `(1 + |Im z|)⁻²`. Exponential sine growth absorbs any polynomial
degree.

newHelpers.name: DLMF.BernoulliEuler.integrable_bernoulliPolyB_mellinBarnes
newHelpers.doc:
The Bernoulli polynomial Mellin–Barnes integrand is integrable on every line `Re z = -c`
with `0 < c < 1`.

newHelpers.name: DLMF.BernoulliEuler.bernoulli_mellinBarnes_line_eq
newHelpers.doc:
Moving the vertical line within `-1 < Re z < 0` preserves the polynomial Mellin–Barnes
integral, by Cauchy’s theorem and uniform decay at infinity.

newHelpers.name: DLMF.BernoulliEuler.bernoulli_mellinBarnes_central_sin
newHelpers.doc: On the central line of the strip, the sine denominator becomes the real hyperbolic cosine.

newHelpers.name: DLMF.BernoulliEuler.bernoulli_mellinBarnes_integral_sech_sq
newHelpers.doc: The zeroth half-line moment of `sech²(πt)` follows from the logistic primitive.

newHelpers.name: DLMF.BernoulliEuler.bernoulli_mellinBarnes_integrable_moment
newHelpers.doc: Every polynomial moment of the central `sech²` kernel is integrable.

newHelpers.name: DLMF.BernoulliEuler.bernoulli_mellinBarnes_even_moment
newHelpers.doc: An even moment of the real `sech²` kernel is twice its integral over the positive half-line.

newHelpers.name: DLMF.BernoulliEuler.bernoulli_mellinBarnes_moment_ofReal
newHelpers.doc:
A moment along the imaginary axis is the corresponding real `sech²` moment multiplied by
the appropriate power of `I`.

newHelpers.name: DLMF.BernoulliEuler.bernoulli_mellinBarnes_moment_two_mul
newHelpers.doc:
The normalized even moments of the central `sech²` kernel evaluate to the Bernoulli
polynomial values at `1/2`, by the known positive half-line integrals.

newHelpers.name: DLMF.BernoulliEuler.bernoulli_mellinBarnes_moment_two_mul_add_one
newHelpers.doc:
Odd moments of the central `sech²` kernel vanish by reflection of the real integration
variable.

newHelpers.name: DLMF.BernoulliEuler.bernoulli_mellinBarnes_moment
newHelpers.doc:
The normalized moments of the central `sech²` kernel are the Bernoulli polynomial values
at `1/2`; odd moments vanish by symmetry.

newHelpers.name: DLMF.BernoulliEuler.bernoulli_mellinBarnes_central_polynomial
newHelpers.doc:
Expanding a polynomial against the central `sech²` kernel gives the Bernoulli addition
formula centered at `1/2`.

newHelpers.name: DLMF.Combinatorics.narayana_choose_catalan_term
newHelpers.doc:
A Catalan convolution term becomes a product of binomial coefficients after multiplication by
`k + 1`. This is the termwise identity used in the Vandermonde sum below.

newHelpers.name: DLMF.Combinatorics.narayana_eq_sum_catalan
newHelpers.doc:
Narayana numbers are a binomial transform of the Catalan numbers, with an additional binomial
coefficient recording the number of peaks.

newHelpers.name: DLMF.Combinatorics.narayana_polynomial_eq_sum_catalan
newHelpers.doc: The Narayana row polynomial is the Catalan transform of the powers of `1 + X`.

newHelpers.name: DLMF.Combinatorics.sum_narayana_mul_pow
newHelpers.doc: The polynomial enumerating a row of the Narayana triangle is a weighted Catalan transform.

newHelpers.name: DLMF.Combinatorics.hasSum_narayana_row
newHelpers.doc:
Each row of the bivariate Narayana series has finite support and can be summed by the
weighted Catalan transform.

newHelpers.name: DLMF.Combinatorics.summable_narayana_mul_pow
newHelpers.doc:
The bivariate Narayana series converges absolutely when both real arguments have absolute
value less than `1/8`.

newHelpers.name: DLMF.Combinatorics.narayana_transform_bounds
newHelpers.doc:
A small square around the origin maps inside the disk of convergence of the Catalan series,
both for the signed argument and for the absolute convergence majorant.

newHelpers.name: DLMF.Combinatorics.narayana_transform_value
newHelpers.doc:
The Catalan generating function simplifies to the Narayana radical formula when the
geometric denominator is positive.

newHelpers.name: DLMF.Combinatorics.hasSum_narayana_of_abs_lt
newHelpers.doc:
The bivariate Narayana generating function on the explicit domain `|x|, |y| < 1/8`, with
`x ≠ 0`. The square root is the branch continuous from the origin.

newHelpers.name: DLMF.Confluent.buchholzC_eq
newHelpers.doc: The normalized Buchholz coefficient is the original coefficient divided by `2^s`.

newHelpers.name: DLMF.Confluent.buchholz_0F1_uniform_bound
newHelpers.doc: The shifted regularized `₀F₁` functions have a factorial bound on each closed disc.

newHelpers.name: DLMF.Confluent.buchholzC_uniform_bound
newHelpers.doc: The factors `z^s` cancel the Cauchy growth of the Taylor coefficients.

newHelpers.name: DLMF.Confluent.buchholzA_uniform_bound
newHelpers.doc: An exponential bound also absorbs the factor `s` in the telescoping coefficient.

newHelpers.name: DLMF.Confluent.buchholzTerm_differentiable
newHelpers.doc: Every Buchholz summand is entire in its argument.

newHelpers.name: DLMF.Confluent.buchholzTerm_uniform_bound
newHelpers.doc: On every disc the Buchholz summands admit a common summable majorant.

newHelpers.name: DLMF.Confluent.buchholz_boundary_tendsto
newHelpers.doc: The boundary term of the Buchholz telescoping relation tends to zero.

newHelpers.name: DLMF.Confluent.buchholzTerm_deriv
newHelpers.doc: Differentiating a normalized Buchholz summand raises the `₀F₁` order by one.

newHelpers.name: DLMF.Confluent.buchholzTerm_second
newHelpers.doc: The second derivative of a Buchholz summand involves only three adjacent `₀F₁` orders.

newHelpers.name: DLMF.Confluent.buchholzTerm_ode
newHelpers.doc:
Applying the normalized Whittaker operator to one Buchholz term gives a telescoping
difference of adjacent orders.

newHelpers.name: DLMF.Confluent.buchholzA_zero
newHelpers.doc: The initial coefficient in the Buchholz telescoping difference vanishes.

newHelpers.name: DLMF.Confluent.buchholz_partial_ode
newHelpers.doc: The partial sums satisfy the normalized Whittaker equation up to a single boundary term.

newHelpers.name: DLMF.Confluent.buchholz_sum_differentiable
newHelpers.doc: The Buchholz series defines an entire function.

newHelpers.name: DLMF.Confluent.buchholz_sum_weighted_ode
newHelpers.doc:
Uniform convergence on a disc is preserved through two complex differentiations, so the
telescoping differential equation passes to the full Buchholz sum.

newHelpers.name: DLMF.Confluent.buchholz_sum_ode
newHelpers.doc: The removable equation at the origin follows by continuity from the punctured plane.

newHelpers.name: DLMF.Confluent.buchholz_normalized_ode_jet
newHelpers.doc: Taylor coefficients of an entire solution satisfy a two-step recurrence at the origin.

newHelpers.name: DLMF.Confluent.buchholz_normalized_ode_zero
newHelpers.doc:
An entire solution of the normalized Whittaker equation vanishes when its initial value
vanishes and the indicial parameter avoids the nonpositive integers.

newHelpers.name: DLMF.Confluent.buchholz_normalized_confluent_ode
newHelpers.doc: Removing the elementary power prefactor from Whittaker M gives the normalized equation.

newHelpers.name: DLMF.Confluent.buchholz_sum_eq_normalized
newHelpers.doc:
The entire Buchholz sum and normalized Whittaker M have the same initial value and satisfy
the same differential equation, so their Taylor series agree.

newHelpers.name: DLMF.QHypergeometric.qPhi_zero
newHelpers.doc: At zero, every unilateral basic hypergeometric series consists only of its constant term.

newHelpers.name: DLMF.QHypergeometric.qPochhammer_root_product
newHelpers.doc: Evaluating Mathlib’s root-of-unity factorization at one gives the finite product.

newHelpers.name: DLMF.QHypergeometric.qPochhammer_prod_roots
newHelpers.doc: Multiplying shifted factorials over all root-of-unity twists raises both parameter and base.

newHelpers.name: DLMF.QHypergeometric.tendsto_cpow_increment
newHelpers.doc: The normalized principal-power increment tends to its exponent as the real base approaches one.

newHelpers.name: DLMF.QHypergeometric.tendsto_qPochhammer_normalized
newHelpers.doc: A normalized finite q-Pochhammer symbol tends to the ordinary rising factorial.

newHelpers.name: DLMF.QHypergeometric.tendsto_qPochhammerList_normalized
newHelpers.doc: The normalized product limit retains the order and multiplicity of upper or lower parameters.

newHelpers.name: DLMF.QHypergeometric.qPochhammerList_normalized_eq
newHelpers.doc: Normalizing each shifted factorial divides the product by the corresponding power.

newHelpers.name: DLMF.QHypergeometric.qPhi_scaling_power
newHelpers.doc: The parameter-count power cancels the singular scaling in a unilateral term.

newHelpers.name: DLMF.QHypergeometric.qPhi_scaling_phase
newHelpers.doc: The signs in the phase and classical argument scaling cancel for every integer exponent.

newHelpers.name: DLMF.QHypergeometric.genPoch_list_ne_zero
newHelpers.doc: A finite ordinary denominator product is nonzero when its retained factors avoid poles.

newHelpers.name: DLMF.QHypergeometric.qPhiTerm_classical_limit
newHelpers.doc: Classical convergence of a single term needs regularity only through that term.

newHelpers.name: DLMF.QHypergeometric.tendsto_qPochhammerList_ratio
newHelpers.doc: Equal-length finite products have a classical ratio limit with no residual power of one minus q.

newHelpers.name: DLMF.QHypergeometric.qPochhammerListInt_neg
newHelpers.doc: A negative-index product is the reciprocal of the appropriately shifted finite product.

newHelpers.name: DLMF.QHypergeometric.qPochhammerInf_factor_at_zero
newHelpers.doc: Removing the vanishing factor of a q-product leaves an analytic unit.

newHelpers.name: DLMF.QHypergeometric.qGauss_coefficient_bound
newHelpers.doc: The phase-free coefficients are bounded because the finite factorials have nonzero limiting denominators.

newHelpers.name: DLMF.QHypergeometric.qGauss_newton_product
newHelpers.doc: Reciprocal upper parameters turn the finite shifted factorial into a Newton polynomial.

newHelpers.name: DLMF.QHypergeometric.qGauss_newton_eq_phi
newHelpers.doc: The Newton series equals two-phi-one at every nonzero reciprocal upper parameter.

newHelpers.name: DLMF.QHypergeometric.qGauss_analytic_newton
newHelpers.doc: The reciprocal-parameter Newton series is analytic throughout its convergence disc.

newHelpers.name: DLMF.QHypergeometric.qGauss_analytic_product
newHelpers.doc: The q-Gauss product quotient is analytic on the same reciprocal-parameter disc.

newHelpers.name: DLMF.QHypergeometric.qGauss_nonzero
newHelpers.doc: Terminating q-Chu values accumulate at zero and determine the analytic q-Gauss identity.

newHelpers.name: DLMF.QHypergeometric.qGauss_poch_zero_base
newHelpers.doc: At base zero, a nonempty finite shifted factorial retains only its first factor.

newHelpers.name: DLMF.QHypergeometric.qGauss_zero_base
newHelpers.doc: At base zero, q-Gauss reduces to summing a geometric tail.

newHelpers.name: DLMF.Struve.lommelRegular_eq_numerator
newHelpers.doc: The regular capital Lommel function is a product of Gamma factors and its entire numerator.

newHelpers.name: DLMF.Struve.lommelNumerator_neg_nat_left
newHelpers.doc: The first half-parameter hyperplane cancels a Gamma pole in the capital Lommel function.

newHelpers.name: DLMF.Struve.lommelNumerator_neg_nat_right
newHelpers.doc: The second half-parameter hyperplane cancels a Gamma pole as well.

newHelpers.name: DLMF.Struve.lommelNumerator_differentiable
newHelpers.doc: The numerator is jointly entire in its two half-parameters.

newHelpers.name: DLMF.Struve.lommel_gamma_backward
newHelpers.doc: The pole-free reciprocal-Gamma shift also gives a totalized backward shift.

newHelpers.name: DLMF.Struve.lommel_gamma_affine_pole
newHelpers.doc: A Gamma pole in an affine half-parameter has one explicit linear denominator.

newHelpers.name: DLMF.Struve.lommel_eventually_affine_regular
newHelpers.doc:
Every punctured affine half-parameter neighborhood consists eventually of Gamma-regular
points, including when the center itself is a pole.

newHelpers.name: DLMF.Struve.lommelNumerator_diagonal_deriv_zero
newHelpers.doc:
At an intersection of the polar hyperplanes, the numerator vanishes to second order along
the degree parameter. The two partial derivatives vanish separately.

newHelpers.name: DLMF.Struve.lommel_tendsto_div_sub
newHelpers.doc: A simple zero cancels one linear denominator in a punctured limit.

newHelpers.name: DLMF.Struve.lommel_exists_tendsto_div_sub_sq
newHelpers.doc:
A double zero cancels two linear denominators; the second divided difference supplies the
finite limiting value.

newHelpers.name: DLMF.Struve.lommelCapital_exists_parameter_limit
newHelpers.doc:
The one- or two-pole numerator cancellations give a finite parameter limit for every
capital Lommel function on the slit plane.

newHelpers.name: DLMF.Weierstrass.HalfPeriods.weierstrassZeta_fourier_bound
newHelpers.doc: Compact subsets of the convergence strip admit a common summable bound for the zeta Fourier terms.

newHelpers.name: DLMF.Weierstrass.HalfPeriods.sin_fourierArgument_ne_zero
newHelpers.doc: A zero of the sine prefactor would lie at a real lattice point.

newHelpers.name: Complex.norm_prod_sub_pow_le
newHelpers.doc:
A geometric Newton polynomial is bounded on a closed disc by its radius to the
polynomial degree, times a constant independent of the degree.

newHelpers.name: Complex.summable_geometricNewton
newHelpers.doc:
Geometrically bounded Newton-series coefficients give a summable series at
every point strictly inside the reciprocal growth radius.

newHelpers.name: Complex.analyticOnNhd_tsum_geometricNewton
newHelpers.doc:
A geometrically bounded series in a geometric Newton basis is analytic on the
open disc given by the reciprocal coefficient growth rate.

statementCorrections.name: DLMF.Weierstrass.HalfPeriods.weierstrassSigma_prod
statementCorrections.reason: At z=0 every normalized product factor is one, but the totalized sigma/prefactor quotient is zero.
statementCorrections.correction: Replace the HasProd-to-quotient conjunct by Multipliable; retain the all-z product identity.
statementCorrections.counterexampleLean:
import DLMF.Weierstrass.Series

open Complex DLMF.Weierstrass
open scoped Real

/-- At z = 0 the normalized sigma-product has value one, rather than its totalized quotient. -/
example (H : HalfPeriods) :
    ¬ HasProd (fun n : ℕ =>
      (1 - 2 * H.nome ^ (2 * (n + 1)) * Complex.cos (π * (0 : ℂ) / H.ω₁) +
        H.nome ^ (4 * (n + 1))) / (1 - H.nome ^ (2 * (n + 1))) ^ 2)
      (H.weierstrassSigma 0 /
        (2 * H.ω₁ / π * cexp (H.eta 1 * (0 : ℂ) ^ 2 / (2 * H.ω₁)) *
          Complex.sin (π * (0 : ℂ) / (2 * H.ω₁)))) := by
  intro h
  have ht (n : ℕ) :
      (1 - 2 * H.nome ^ (2 * (n + 1)) * Complex.cos (π * (0 : ℂ) / H.ω₁) +
        H.nome ^ (4 * (n + 1))) / (1 - H.nome ^ (2 * (n + 1))) ^ 2 = 1 := by
    have hn : 1 - H.nome ^ (2 * (n + 1)) ≠ 0 :=
      DLMF.QSeries.one_sub_ne_zero_of_norm_lt_one
        (DLMF.Theta.p20R1_norm_nome_pow_lt_one H.tau_im_pos (by omega))
    simp only [mul_zero, zero_div, Complex.cos_zero, mul_one]
    rw [show H.nome ^ (4 * (n + 1)) = (H.nome ^ (2 * (n + 1))) ^ 2 by rw [← pow_mul]; ring_nf]
    field_simp
    ring
  simp only [mul_zero, zero_div, Complex.sin_zero, div_zero] at h
  have h1 : HasProd (fun _ : ℕ => (1 : ℂ)) 0 := h.congr_fun (fun n => by simpa using (ht n).symm)
  exact zero_ne_one (h1.unique hasProd_one)
